subject: Private VPC onboarding — network ownership, allowlist window, and SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC onboarding — network ownership, allowlist window, and SOC2 evidence

Thanks for the call this morning, Ethan — good to meet you and the Vantage team. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned while we scope the Private VPC deployment:

1) Deployment mode decision
- You confirmed interest in a Private VPC (private endpoint + tenant isolation) for PHI workloads. We noted Dedicated and Hosted are options for non-PHI tiers but VPC is the requirement for production PHI.

2) Network ownership & allowlist
- Vantage NetOps will need to provide either a PrivateLink endpoint (preferred) or VPC peering. If PrivateLink: please provide the account ID and target subnet CIDR ranges. If peering: we need the VPC IDs and routing/contact for peering approvals.
- Allowlist window: we typically coordinate a 2-hour maintenance window for initial traffic validation (egress IPs will be provided). Please confirm preferred dates in the Dec 6–10 or Dec 13–17 windows.

3) Security evidence (SOC2 / audit items)
- You asked for SOC2-related artifacts: we can share a SOC2 snapshot and SOC2 contact for the security questionnaire redline items. I've attached a redacted SOC2 snapshot and a simple network diagram for the PrivateLink flow.

4) Owner matrix + timeline
- Suggested owners: Vantage NetOps for allowlist + peering setup; Redwood for endpoint provisioning and initial validation. Proposed timeline after confirmation: 1 week for endpoint provisioning + allowlist setup, 2–3 business days for validation.

5) Action items (owners / due)
- Ethan: confirm PrivateLink vs peering decision and preferred allowlist window (Reply by Tue, 2026-11-30).
- Vantage NetOps: provide account ID/VPC IDs and firewall egress rules for review.
- Marissa (CS): will coordinate the provisioning slot and run validation.

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram.png (PNG — PrivateLink flow), SOC2-snapshot-Q3-2026.pdf (PDF — redacted).

Thanks — I’ll hold a provisional slot the week of Dec 6 until I hear back.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(aditya.rao@redwood.ai)

Aditya — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Couple items: 

- We prefer PrivateLink (sits better with our security team).
- NetOps will supply the target subnet CIDRs and our AWS account ID by Monday (11/30).
- For allowlist window we prefer Dec 14 morning (08:00–10:00 PT). That gives our SRE time to prep.

Two quick questions from NetOps (cc’d):
1) What are the exact egress IP addresses we should allow?
2) Do you expect any outgoing connections from our VPC to Redwood-managed services beyond the PrivateLink endpoint (for telemetry/metrics)?

We’re aiming to have procurement sign-off early next week so timeline looks feasible.

—Ethan

Hi netops — looping in the technical owners on our side. Answers inline to your two questions and a few asks below:

> 1) What are the exact egress IP addresses we should allow?

We provide a short-lived set of egress IPs for the initial validation. For the Dec 14 window the provisional egress set is: 34.210.12.48, 18.204.77.122, 34.201.59.200. These are NAT egress addresses used during validation; final production egress may differ if you choose peering vs PrivateLink. We will send a formal allowlist CSV 48 hours before the window.

> 2) Do you expect any outgoing connections from our VPC to Redwood-managed services beyond the PrivateLink endpoint (for telemetry/metrics)?

Short answer: no external outbound connections are required for inference traffic when using PrivateLink. We will exchange metrics over the PrivateLink channel. Two exceptions: optional telemetry for deeper observability (metrics to prometheus.redwood.ai) and scheduled OS patching callbacks if you opt into our managed node package. Both are opt-in and can be disabled.

Additional asks:
- Please share Vantage AWS account ID and 3 target subnet CIDRs by EOD Mon (11/30) so we can pre-configure the endpoint.
- Please confirm who will sign the provisioning ticket in NetOps (name + email).

I’ve attached the same SOC2 snapshot and a more detailed diagram showing the PrivateLink flow and the validation traffic pattern.

If Dec 14 works we’ll provision on Dec 11 and run validation on the 14th.

Thanks,
Aditya
